title: Hassock (Rockaway Beach)
summary: Hassock is recorded by Tooker as a creek in the meadow near Rockaway Beach. The exact creek has not been identified, but the name is associated broadly with the Rockaway Beach marsh landscape.
address_label: Rockaway Beach, Queens County, New York
map_geometry_source: Approximate general location based on Tooker identifying a creek in the meadow near Rockaway Beach; not an exact historic coordinate.
history_content: This Hassock entry belongs to a small group of marsh and meadow names near Rockaway and East Rockaway Inlet. The specific creek and Coast Survey sheet still need review before the location can be narrowed.
translation_content:
Hassock is connected with Algonquian words for marshy ground. The same source compares Narragansett hassucki, meaning marsh land, and Delaware assisku, meaning miry or marshy. The spelling also appears in early records in forms such as Hassokie and Hassokey for similar meadow or swamp places.

Why Place Names Matter

“When the direct record, in later days, is of the meagrest, place names may be found to offer definite evidence on important points.”

— James B. Johnston, The Place-Names of England and Wales (1915), Internet Archive scan leaf 553
land_loss_content: This placename preserves a marsh vocabulary tied to creeks, meadows, and wet ground along the Rockaway shore. Recording it with uncertainty helps distinguish the Indigenous-language placename from later shoreline changes and modern map labels.
whereintheworld_content: The point shown is an approximate general marker for the Rockaway Beach meadow and marsh landscape, placed near the Jamaica Bay side of the Rockaway peninsula. It is not an exact historic creek coordinate.
